pool.text: Traveler Ainsworth estimated the small borough of Ahvaz was inhabited by fifteen hundred people.
The Karun river in late Qajar Iran was dredged and reopened to commerce.
Curzon documented the population of the small borough of Ahvaz at seven hundred inhabitants.
The provincial government of Khuzestan province was officially transferred to Ahvaz from Shushtar.
The Trans-Iranian Railway successfully reached the interior location of Ahvaz.
The Council of Ministers approved officially naming the city Ahvaz once again.
Pol Sefid arch bridge was completed and inaugurated in the city.
A refugee camp for Polish refugees was established inside Ahvaz.
Gondishapur University was founded before being renamed Jundishapur shortly afterwards.
The first cohort of agriculture faculty graduates received their certificates at a ceremony.
Iraq attempted to annex Khuzestan and Ahvaz, sparking the Iran-Iraq War.
Azad University Ahvaz Branch was established as the first provincial branch.
The Foolad Ahvaz steel facility was built near the town.
Foolad F.C. won the championship of Iran's Premier Football League.
The World Health Organization ranked Ahvaz as the world's most air-polluted city.
Foolad won the football league for the second time during this season.
Thousands of aircraft took off and landed at the local airport moving cargo and passengers.
Esteghlal Khuzestan won the top football league for the very first time.
Gunmen killed at least twenty nine people at the military parade attack.
Iraqi militias affiliated with the Iranian government recruited forces to suppress protests.
